report:
**Conclusion:**  
High-quality clinical evidence demonstrates that saw palmetto (*Serenoa repens*) preparations **do not** significantly improve lower urinary tract symptoms or objective measures (such as peak urine flow) in men with benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) compared to placebo over the longer term.

### Summary of Research Evidence

* **Cochrane Systematic Reviews:** Meta-analyses of randomized controlled trials evaluating long-term outcomes (12 to 17+ months) found high-certainty evidence that saw palmetto is no more effective than placebo at reducing urologic symptoms or improving quality of life [https://www.cochrane.org/evidence/CD001423_serenoa-repens-benign-prostatic-hyperplasia], [https://www.aafp.org/afp/2024/0500/cochrane-saw-palmetto-benign-prostatic-hyperplasia].
* **Dose-Escalation Long-Term Studies:** The landmark CAMUS randomized controlled trial investigated long-term saw palmetto use over 72 weeks (18 months), increasing the dose up to three times the standard amount (960 mg/day). The study found no statistically or clinically significant benefit over placebo in symptom scores or maximum urine flow rates [https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jama/fullarticle/1104439].

In summary, rigorous long-term trials consistently conclude that saw palmetto extracts provide no meaningful therapeutic benefit over placebo for BPH symptoms.
